s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of severe upper abdominal pain with associated nausea and vomiting, worsened by oral intake, in a post-surgical patient
salient_findings: Sudden-onset, sharp upper abdominal pain rated 9/10
Pain worsened with oral intake
Associated nausea and vomiting
Generalized abdominal tenderness, most pronounced in the right hypochondrium
CT findings of clustered small-bowel loops and spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels
key_facts: 36-year-old woman presented with acute abdominal pain
Pain awakened her early in the morning
Pain was minimally relieved by oxycodone
Patient had undergone Roux-en-Y gastric bypass three weeks earlier
Patient had intermittent nausea after gastric bypass
Patient denied bloating, changes in bowel habits, or urinary symptoms
Medical history included type 2 diabetes mellitus
Patient had undergone multiple abdominal surgeries
Vital signs were within normal limits
Laboratory studies showed normal liver function tests and lactate level
CT scan demonstrated no signs of anastomotic leak, strangulation, or bowel obstruction

shortlist.label: Internal hernia
shortlist.why_kept: CT findings of clustered small-bowel loops and spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels

shortlist.label: Adhesional bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's extensive surgical history and symptoms of bowel obstruction

shortlist.label: Intestinal obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting

shortlist.label: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complication
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's recent history of gastric bypass surgery and symptoms of bowel obstruction

shortlist.label: Small bowel strangulation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of severe abdominal pain and CT findings of congestion of mesenteric fat

raw.rationale: The CT scan demonstrated a cluster of small-bowel loops in the left upper quadrant with a spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels, congestion of mesenteric fat, and stretching and convergence of vessels, which is consistent with internal hernia, particularly given the patient's recent history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass.

rejected.label: Adhesional bowel obstruction
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of multiple abdominal surgeries, the CT findings and the specific pattern of bowel loop clustering and mesenteric vessel arrangement are more suggestive of internal hernia than adhesional bowel obstruction.

rejected.label: Intestinal obstruction
rejected.why: The CT scan did not show signs of bowel obstruction, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complication
rejected.why: While the patient's recent surgery is relevant, the specific findings on the CT scan point more directly to an internal hernia as the cause of her symptoms rather than a general complication of the bypass surgery.

rejected.label: Small bowel strangulation
rejected.why: There were no signs of strangulation on the CT scan, which makes this diagnosis unlikely given the information provided.
